Dog Friendly Bright, Victoria: Cafes, Pubs, Walks & Stays

By | October 23, 2026 | 0

Bright is one of Victoria’s most dog-friendly towns. Set on the Ovens River in the Victorian High Country, about 320 km north-east of Melbourne, it welcomes dogs at riverside cafes, a local brewery, holiday rentals and a network of walking tracks. If you’re looking for dog friendly Bright options, the easiest starting point is the Ovens River. The Canyon Walk (about 3 km, easy grade) and the Cherry Walk both start near Howitt Park and Centenary Park in the town centre. Dogs can go off-leash on parts of both tracks and must be on a lead elsewhere, so check the signs and the Alpine Shire Council map before you let them off.

For dog friendly cafes in Bright, you’ll find outdoor seating in the town centre and nearby Porepunkah and Myrtleford. Venues like Cafe Fez in Myrtleford is particularly dog friendly with treats on offer for their furry customers. For dog friendly bars in Bright, Bright Brewery has dog-friendly outdoor tables. Beyond town, Dinner Plain is one of the few alpine villages in Australia that welcomes dogs.

This guide covers the best dog friendly cafes, bars and pubs, off-leash and on-leash walks, and dog friendly stays in Bright, with leash rules checked against Alpine Shire Council. Updated October 2026.

KNOW BEFORE YOU GO — OFFICIAL LEASH RULES

Alpine Shire Council requires dogs to be on-lead within designated town centre areas, as shown on the official on-lead maps on the Alpine Shire Council website. Outside those zones, dogs may be off-lead but must be under effective control at all times — meaning they return immediately on command, remain in clear sight, and don’t bother other people or animals. There are no formal fenced off-leash dog parks in Bright. Always check current signage on the day, as rules can change.

Pet & Dog Friendly Accommodation in Bright

Abbeville Cottage

Bright

Enjoy a relaxing stay at Abbeville, a charming pet friendly holiday home just a short stroll from Bright’s cafés, restaurants and riverside walks. With plenty of space for families and dogs, it’s the perfect base to explore Victoria’s High Country.

Amber Mist Villa Two

Bright

Stay just moments from the heart of Bright in this modern pet friendly villa, featuring a secure fenced yard, dogs welcome inside, and easy access to cafés, the Ovens River and scenic walking trails. A perfect base for couples, families and unforgettable High Country adventures.

Dog Friendly Cafes in Bright & Surrounds

Cafe Fez

145 Great Alpine Road, Myrtleford

Cafe Fez in Myrtleford is where Moroccan magic meets tail-wagging good times! Step into a world of twinkling lanterns, silver teapots and rich, colourful textiles — it’s basically a mini escape to Fez or Safi, minus the plane ticket (and your pup’s totally invited). Sink into a low-slung cushioned booth with your favourite human or gather the crew, tuck into Middle-Eastern favourites, and sip on a Moroccan mint tea poured with proper theatre — three pours, straight from a silver tray.

While you’re soaking up the ambience, your dog can tuck into a healthy kangaroo treats, because good vibes should be shared by the whole family. Open daily for breakfast and lunch, this chilled-out gem is equal parts cosy and exotic. Grab the lead and your best mate — Cafe Fez is calling, and it’s unlike anywhere else in Myrtleford!

Rail Trail Cafe

2 Service Street, Porepunkah

Just 6km from Bright and situated on the popular Murray to Mountains Rail Trail, the cafe has a relaxing outdoor dining area where dogs are more than welcome. Water bowls are provided to keep pups cool and hydrated.

Dog Friendly Pubs & Bars in Bright & Surrounds

Bright Brewery

121 Great Alpine Road, Bright

Bright Brewery is a mountain town brewery, and so, naturally, they use only fresh mountain water in their brews. The brewery door is open daily and features a 24-tap bar, which is especially impressive — even for a brewery.

Mountain Monk Brewery

1 Lakeside Avenue, Mount Beauty

Previously known as West Peak Hotel, Mountain Monk Brewers is a craft brewery and pub located in Mount Beauty, Victoria. With ten beers on tap, brewed right on site, Mountain Monk Brewers offers something for everyone, from classic lagers and ales to more adventurous sours and fruit beers. Dogs are always welcome to join you at the outdoor seating area.

Tomahawks

15 Camp Street, Bright

Tomahawks is a casual bar and all day eatery in beautiful Bright, North East Victoria. Serving quality food, booze and good times, Tomahawks is a favourite for both locals and visitors alike.There are tables under the front verandah where dogs can join their owners for a drink or a meal. 

Don Mungo’s

90 Gavan Street

Dog Friendly Bar Don Mungo’s is serving up some of the best Pizza around, along with a solid beer list, signature cocktails and live music, this really is the place to be. Dog Friendly Beer Garden included!

Dog Friendly Walks in Bright & Surrounds

SEASONAL NOTE

Summer temperatures in Bright regularly exceed 35°C — the Ovens River becomes the dog’s best friend. Always carry water, plan walks for early morning, and use the river access points generously. In autumn (April–May), Bright transforms into one of Australia’s great colour spectacles as the elm and plane trees turn. The cooler temperatures make autumn the best walking season of the year, and the Canyon Walk in autumn light is genuinely something to behold.

AUTUMN

The famous leaf fall turns Bright into a living painting. Cool, crisp and perfect for longer walks — the Canyon Walk in autumn light is something else entirely.

WINTER

Cold but magical. Snow trips up to Dinner Plain are the ultimate dog adventure — one of Australia’s only alpine villages that welcomes dogs in winter.

SPRING

Wildflowers, fresh creeks and a reborn landscape. Quiet season means more trail to yourselves — and the Ovens starts to warm up for early swimmers.

SUMMER

Hot days, crystal-clear swimming holes and long evenings at the Bright Brewery. Hit the trails at dawn and claim the river by 10am.

Cherry Walk

Bright

A gentler amble along the Ovens River beginning at Howitt Park, heading east past the Splash Park. Dogs must remain on-lead through Howitt Park and Centenary Park — once past Centenary Park, off-lead under effective control applies for the remainder of the walk. Mostly flat and well-formed, it suits all ages and breeds.

Canyon Walk

Bright

The undisputed highlight of Bright’s walk network. This track follows the Ovens River through a dramatic canyon carved out by gold sluicing in the 1850s — all swinging bridges, mossy boulders and river crossings. Dogs must be on-lead from the Howitt Park end until the end of Riverside Avenue, after which off-lead under effective control applies for the bulk of the canyon section. In summer the river pools are perfect for a mid-walk splash. One of the best dog walks in regional Victoria.

The Diggins Loop

Wandiligong

A short drive from Bright, this loop through the historic Wandiligong goldfields sits outside any gazetted on-lead zone — dogs are off-lead under effective control throughout. Old mining relics dot the landscape and Morses Creek provides natural doggy hydration at regular intervals.

Porepunkah River Walk

Porepunkah

A quieter, easygoing option just outside Bright, hugging the banks of the Ovens River through paddock and bush. Mainly on-lead through the Porepunkah township area — check local signage. Wonderfully peaceful, and a natural add-on if you’re cycling or walking the rail trail.
